children: has overhauled its Copilot assistant, merging its enterprise and consumer versions into a more capable product featuring agents allowing individuals and organizations to better scale AI work.
The tech titan has worked on the engineering overhaul of the product for the past six months. The efforts were
several months ago, but the new product begins rolling out today through its Frontier program, Microsoft announced.

The Copilot app now includes Home, which brings together Chat and Cowork. It features Code as well, which allows users to build and run software powered by GitHub Copilot technology. It also has Autopilot, formerly called Scout, which functions as a proactive and persistent personal agent.
Finally, and maybe most important for some enterprises, is the introduction of FinOps for AI. This helps clients better understand and manage the amount being spent on AI tools.

"FinOps for AI is a shared discipline for managing AI spend and optimizing it for business value," said Jared Spataro, chief marketing officer for Microsoft AI at Work, in a Friday blog post. "We are committed to enabling organizations to make the most of their AI spend, and, today, we are introducing new capabilities across Agent 365, Insights and Microsoft Copilot to help do that … Admins can manage spending policies at scale with API access; route credit requests from end users into existing approval and automation workflows; and set which model families are available to different groups of users—those settings also shape which models Auto can select from."

Although individual users can still access and use the new Copilot, this new version has a particular focus on serving corporate clients. However, the incorporation of some features from the consumer app has apparently improved its usability. It also arrives as Meta
appears to be gaining steam with its personal AI agent app, Muse. And this week, Qualcomm
released a slate of new platforms built to run personal agents on an array of devices.
Microsoft plans to reveal more features coming to Copilot at its Ignite event, which runs from November 17 to 20 in San Francisco.

title: Microsoft revamps Copilot with focus on enterprise clients, AI spend management
